sources.entry: Burette - Molecular workspace and Finder Quick Look extension for macOS: 3D structures, chemistry grids, and local workflow-artifact inspection.

summary.one_liner: Burette is a macOS app and Finder Quick Look extension for previewing and inspecting molecular structure files in 3D, browsing chemistry collections, and sketching molecules.
summary.what_it_does: Press Space on a supported molecular file in Finder to get a preview, or open the full Burette workspace to view structures in tabs with a project sidebar. Structures render through Mol* for interactive 3D, while SDF, SMILES, CSV and TSV files open in an RDKit-powered collection grid with search, sorting, SMARTS filtering, and export. The desktop app includes a Ketcher small-molecule sketcher, a Chemical Space view for similarity mapping, and trajectory controls for MD topology and trajectory pairs. It also has workflow panels for superposition, docking pose review, and FEP network previews. A source-built iPhone preview target and a hosted MCP plugin for ChatGPT or Codex are also described in the README.
use_cases: preview molecular files in Finder with Quick Look
browse and filter compound collections by properties
sketch small molecules and send them to a viewer
review docking poses and superimpose structures
open molecular files on an iPhone from Files
how_to_run: Open Burette.app once from Applications so the Quick Look extension registers
In Finder, select a supported molecular file and press Space
bun run install:plugin (installs the local Codex plugin from the repository)
notable: Finder Quick Look extension for previewing molecular files with the Space key
Supports over a dozen structure, trajectory, volume, and mass spectrometry formats through Mol*, RDKit, and xyzrender paths
Built-in Ketcher sketcher with import/export and handoff to viewers and grids
Codex plugin with typed local MCP server and allowlisted Mol* actions
Native Apple Silicon compute for clustering, similarity search, conformers, and Chemical Space embeddings
caveats: Current macOS release bundles require Apple Silicon and macOS 12 or later
Macromolecule editing is not enabled in the Ketcher integration
The iPhone app is not in the Homebrew release and must be built from source with Xcode
Public plugin installation through OpenAI's Plugins Directory depends on directory review and is not yet available
